# What does multimodal alignment align: vectors, visual interfaces, or evidence dependence?

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/multimodal-models/alignment-interfaces.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-18 · 29 topic entries / 15 representative comparisons

CLIP and EmbeddingGemma 2 produce comparable vectors. BLIP-2 and LLaVA connect vision to conditional generation, CV-OPD trains visual evidence use, and UMRM scores responses. Their supervision and interfaces differ, not a single capability ladder.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### A shared retrieval space is not a language input space

CLIP and EmbeddingGemma 2 align vector similarities; the latter supports selected MRL dimensions. BLIP-2 queries and LLaVA projections condition an LLM and require generative training to use them. Matching dimensions or retrieval semantics do not make a vector a general-purpose visual soft prompt.

Sources: [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md) · [BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en.md) · [Visual Instruction Tuning](../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en.md)

### A good-looking answer and genuine image evidence use differ

UMRM learns rewards from caption perturbations and checks selection of policy-generated responses, rather than only hand-built negatives. CV-OPD changes teacher crops under a fixed student prefix to constrain distributions directly. Evaluation and distillation can complement each other without a reward benchmark proving visual attribution.

Sources: [Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling](../../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en.md) · [CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation](../../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en.md) · [Visual Instruction Tuning](../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en.md)

### October 29: publication update and evidence boundary

The formal EmbeddingGemma 2 paper is the October 6 model, not a new identity. It describes pooling 512-dimensional backbone features then projecting to 768. Pinned official code projects before returning `last_hidden_state`; equal-weight masked means commute with that linear map. Keep the 16-image GPU result at its prior evidence grade, not audio/video or seven-benchmark acceptance.

Sources: [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md)

### Speech embeddings, discrete speech units, and translation candidates are different output interfaces

EmbeddingGemma 2 maps multiple modalities to comparable fixed-width vectors, with MRL reducing vector width. GSLM2 extracts several time-aligned discrete streams from the same speech, so joint deduplication changes sequence length; its stream-specific heads score spoken candidates conditioned on shared history. NaijaS2ST instead requires cross-language speech generation and evaluates it with translation references and ASR-COMET. Vector neighbors, same-language paired discrimination and cross-language generation cannot share one accuracy measure. The local GSLM2 slice verifies transformations of supplied units and probabilities, not real speech capability.

Sources: [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md) · [GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en.md) · [NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages](../../../../multimodal-models/2604.16287-naijas2st/README-en.md)

### Interface alignment is not cultural understanding: identify outputs and shortcuts first

AVMeme Exam asks models to interpret audio in multilingual, multicultural contexts and handles non-target shortcuts through text_cheat and visual_cheat. MMEB-V3 instead evaluates external embedding rankings for semantic relevance, requested modality and task coverage. Both require clean evaluation boundaries, but denominators, candidate spaces and outputs differ. Anonymous upload fields and private answer mappings constrain the protocol only. If question text, file permissions or pretraining leak answers, L0 field checks neither rule out contamination nor establish reliable cultural judgment.

Sources: [AVMeme Exam: A Multimodal Multilingual Multicultural Benchmark for LLMs' Contextual and Cultural Knowledge and Thinking](../../../../multimodal-models/2601.17645-avmeme-exam/README-en.md) · [MMEB-V3: Measuring the Performance Gaps of Omni-Modality Embedding Models](../../../../multimodal-models/2604.23321-mmeb-v3/README-en.md)

### Semantic alignment and modality adherence are separate acceptance axes

OmniSET retains semantically equivalent T/I/V/A candidates in one shared pool, including the query itself as a distractor. Correctness requires both semantics and target modality. Target-modality prefiltering removes the collapse it is meant to expose. MVEB emphasizes video tasks, eight retrieval directions and model-specific frame/audio budgets; aggregates are not interchangeable. Both complete matrices are expensive. This round verifies MMEB-V3 scoring only, while MVEB remains review-only rather than disguising a generic aggregator as two complete integrations.

Sources: [MMEB-V3: Measuring the Performance Gaps of Omni-Modality Embedding Models](../../../../multimodal-models/2604.23321-mmeb-v3/README-en.md) · [MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark](../../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en.md)

### Visual interface placement and dedicated capacity are different variables

Unbundling inserts extra capacity into joint attention/FFNs; BLIP-2 extracts visual information with learned queries before a frozen LLM. Check the visual mask rather than modality isolation for the former, and frozen boundaries/query bottlenecks for the latter. Initial functional equality is not trained capability equality, and the existing small BLIP-2 negative result is not the new paper's large-model comparison.

Sources: [Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding](../../../../foundation-models/2611.17334-unbundling-vision/README-en.md) · [BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en.md)

### Shared alignment does not replace private-information preservation

Alignment constrains retained information; it does not automatically preserve everything needed downstream. Visual details and question relations may need private fibers; omitting private–private decorrelation permits coordination. Local loss/gradient tests do not measure actual synergy, and existing Fashion-MNIST CLIP results are not matched-paper comparisons.

Sources: [Asymmetric Multimodal Learning with Decomposed JEPAs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.16639-d-jepa/README-en.md) · [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md)

### Shared-space matching and cross-space translation impose different geometry

First identify the space of each score operand and which sides receive gradients. Duo compares translated sources with own targets, whereas CLIP compares own representations directly. Skipless removes identity shortcuts and needs dedicated initialization. The local single-head layer omits full LeJEPA and global negatives, so it does not reproduce unaligned medical-retrieval geometry.

Sources: [DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces](../../../../foundation-models/2611.15968-duojepa/README-en.md) · [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md)

### Estimator bias and multimodal alignment geometry are different axes

InfoNCE negative counts affect more than variance: under misspecification they can change surrogate optima. Non-contrastive squared-covariance plug-ins can be biased through same-sample terms. Audit geometry, objectives, independent sampling and optimization budgets separately rather than infer cost/capability from labels. There is no source empirical matrix and no invented expensive deferred experiment.

Sources: [Spectral Ghost in Representation Learning: A Unified View from Component Analysis to Self-Supervised Learning](../../../../foundation-models/2601.20154-spectral-ghost/README-en.md) · [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md)

### Alignment training, local retrieval and database throughput need separate validation

CLIP similarities come from contrastively learned global image/text representations. Page multivector late interaction preserves each query token's best local evidence. Similarity is not relevance probability and requires sealed independent judgments. The library paper conflicts on preencoded database versus end-to-end concurrency scope, so local timing requires an explicit scope and true wall-clock QPS rather than treating Table VII as reproduced model throughput.

Sources: [Towards High-Performance Multimodal Discovery: Evaluating Retrieval Efficacy and Operational Scalability in Digital Libraries](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.17726-multimodal-library-protocol/README-en.md) · [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md)

### Speech representation scores and call-decision risks belong to different layers

The GSLM2 slice jointly deduplicates changing streams and scores transitions, leaving the model external. The FEND slice arbitrates timestamped external events without audio detectors. Wait for the priority window and use true humans for HFPR. The paper's 0.979 is human-versus-rest F1; AI-class F1 is only 0.571, not solved four-class detection.

Sources: [FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.18050-fend-protocol/README-en.md) · [GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### Why doesn't correct image retrieval with CLIP or EmbeddingGemma 2 show LLaVA can answer image questions? {#cross-embedding-versus-answer}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Retrieval matches candidate representations. LLaVA generates answer tokens from an image, question, and context, which needs a generative interface and supervision. Compare the same output task, not retrieval hits pooled with answer correctness.

    **Illustrative example:** Retrieving an image of cups does not establish counting them, citing evidence, or following an answer format.

    Sources: [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md) · [Visual Instruction Tuning](../../../../reproductions/2304.08485-llava/README-en.md)

### Do fewer BLIP-2 queries and narrower EmbeddingGemma 2 vectors save the same resource? {#cross-two-compression-axes}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Q-Former queries determine visual sequence length to the LLM. MRL width affects retrieval-vector storage and similarity. Both can lose information but at different stages; use trained prefixes with renormalization, not coordinate deletion as visual pooling.

    **Illustrative example:** Thirty-two visual tokens and a 256-dimensional vector are length and width, not directly comparable.

    Sources: [BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md)

### Does UMRM detecting a caption color perturbation show the CV-OPD student uses the right image region? {#cross-reward-versus-visual-dependence}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** UMRM ranks one negative distribution, while policy errors can differ. CV-OPD compares student and positive/negative crop teachers on a shared prefix. Correct judging, receiving that training signal, and genuinely changing evidence use are separate checks.

    **Illustrative example:** A judge spotting red changed to blue does not show the student stopped guessing common colors.

    Sources: [Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling](../../../../reproductions/2610.12707-umrm/README-en.md) · [CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation](../../../../reproductions/2610.13264-cv-opd/README-en.md)

### When can prior results survive a difference between paper and code operator order? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Check the actual operations. The same bias-free linear projection commutes with equal-weight masked averaging and the pinned code/checkpoint did not change. Nonlinearity, different weights, or retraining do not inherit equivalence. Only provenance changes here.

    **Illustrative example:** `mean(W h1,W h2)=W mean(h1,h2)`; averaging two GELU outputs generally does not equal GELU of their mean.

    Sources: [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md) · [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md)

### To compare which spoken continuation is more plausible, can a unified audio embedding similarity replace GSLM2's transition score? {#cross-nov07-speech-stream-versus-embedding}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** They are not equivalent. EmbeddingGemma 2's fixed vector supports object similarity. GSLM2's score uses sequential conditional probabilities at first and changed positions per stream, then weights streams equally. Continuations can match the same topic while differing in grammar or phonetic transitions. Translation needs a separate cross-language protocol such as NaijaS2ST.

    **Illustrative example:** Example: Two endings mention a cup and may be close in embedding space, but only one uses the right verb form in context. Compare sequence scores and retrieval similarity separately; do not report the latter as sBLIMP accuracy.

    Sources: [EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations](../../../../multimodal-models/embeddinggemma2/README-en.md) · [GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en.md) · [NaijaS2ST: A Multi-Accent Benchmark for Speech-to-Speech Translation in Low-Resource Nigerian Languages](../../../../multimodal-models/2604.16287-naijas2st/README-en.md)

### If AVMeme's main-split filtering and MMEB-V3's mixed-pool checks pass, does multimodal capability improve? {#cross-cross-cultural-answer-versus-retrieval-interface}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Passing checks establishes declared sample and candidate protocols only. Real models, fixed authorized data, complete task metrics and independent comparisons remain necessary. Cultural answering and embedding retrieval must be reported separately; protocol success or a fixture score of one is not capability improvement.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: an always-A callback can pass answer-field isolation without hearing audio. A handwritten ranking can retrieve the right modality without being an encoder prediction.

    Sources: [AVMeme Exam: A Multimodal Multilingual Multicultural Benchmark for LLMs' Contextual and Cultural Knowledge and Thinking](../../../../multimodal-models/2601.17645-avmeme-exam/README-en.md) · [MMEB-V3: Measuring the Performance Gaps of Omni-Modality Embedding Models](../../../../multimodal-models/2604.23321-mmeb-v3/README-en.md)

### Why is audio-prefiltering OmniSET unfair even if Hit@1 improves? {#cross-cross-omniset-prefilter-hides-failure}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** It changes the task by satisfying output modality on the model's behalf and hides preference for the query itself or another modality. All twelve directions must share the mixed pool. MVEB input-budget controls do not replace this candidate protocol.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: an image-to-audio model always ranks the original image first. Audio filtering makes it appear successful by removing its original instruction-following failure.

    Sources: [MMEB-V3: Measuring the Performance Gaps of Omni-Modality Embedding Models](../../../../multimodal-models/2604.23321-mmeb-v3/README-en.md) · [MVEB: Massive Video Embedding Benchmark](../../../../multimodal-models/2606.14958-mveb/README-en.md)

### Why not rank Unbundling against BLIP-2 simply by visual token count? {#cross-nov15-unbundling-vision}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** BLIP-2 studies a query bottleneck between frozen models. Unbundling separates dedicated capacity, priors and placement while retaining joint attention. Token counts, trainable parameters and lifetime budgets differ and need matched experiments.

    **Illustrative example:** Four queries can reduce tokens but lose details. Early vision-only FFNs add capacity without directly reducing tokens; these are not interchangeable benefits.

    Sources: [Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding](../../../../foundation-models/2611.17334-unbundling-vision/README-en.md) · [BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models](../../../../reproductions/2301.12597-blip2/README-en.md)

### Does D-JEPA establish that CLIP-style alignment is always wrong? {#cross-nov15-d-jepa}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. It concerns informational asymmetry and exactly aligned solutions, while CLIP also performs instance discrimination and retrieval. Match models, data and readouts before claiming task-information loss.

    **Illustrative example:** Different questions about one scene are not equally informative views; image–caption retrieval has a different supervision structure.

    Sources: [Asymmetric Multimodal Learning with Decomposed JEPAs](../../../../foundation-models/2611.16639-d-jepa/README-en.md) · [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md)

### Why not replace DuoJEPA's bidirectional InfoNCE with CLIP loss? {#cross-nov15-duojepa}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** CLIP compares own vectors. Each Duo term compares a translated source with an own centroid inside one target space. Replacing it changes geometry, centroid construction and encoder gradients.

    **Illustrative example:** An own image vector is in image space; its translated version is in text space. The latter matches the own text vector.

    Sources: [DuoJEPA: Cross-Modal Translation Between Unaligned Self-Supervised Embedding Spaces](../../../../foundation-models/2611.15968-duojepa/README-en.md) · [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md)

### Does unbiasedness analysis prove smaller CLIP batches are better? {#cross-nov15-spectral-ghost}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Unbiasedness differs from variance, statistical efficiency and misspecification; a fixed-negative ranking-NCE surrogate has its own optimum. Objective theory is not a downstream performance ranking.

    **Illustrative example:** Removing same-sample bias can still leave large finite-batch variance. Accuracy and convergence need experiments that this paper does not supply.

    Sources: [Spectral Ghost in Representation Learning: A Unified View from Component Analysis to Self-Supervised Learning](../../../../foundation-models/2601.20154-spectral-ghost/README-en.md) · [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md)

### Does a MaxSim toy example beating a distractor show that it is better than CLIP for real libraries? {#cross-nov18-multimodal-library-protocol}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. It only validates readout arithmetic. Real comparison needs matched pages/queries, audited judgments, encoding/reranking settings and budgets, separating model quality, index recall and serving performance. CLIP's small-task result is not long-document page capability either.

    **Illustrative example:** Two query tokens may match two page patches for score 2, but that says neither whether relevant pages are fully indexed nor what throughput includes ColPali inference.

    Sources: [Towards High-Performance Multimodal Discovery: Evaluating Retrieval Efficacy and Operational Scalability in Digital Libraries](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.17726-multimodal-library-protocol/README-en.md) · [Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision](../../../../reproductions/2103.00020-clip/README-en.md)

### Does FEND's 0.979 human-versus-rest F1 establish that a multi-stream speech model detects AI speech well? {#cross-cross-nov18-fend-protocol}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Binary F1 is not AI-class F1 or representation quality. FEND additionally depends on commercial ASR, tools and timing models. GSLM2 addresses different tasks; each needs its own frozen protocol and real model outputs.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: low human rejection can coexist with AI mislabeled voicemail, retaining high binary F1 but poor four-way discrimination.

    Sources: [FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.18050-fend-protocol/README-en.md) · [GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling](../../../../multimodal-models/2611.01143-gslm2/README-en.md)
